evidence.note: When score dropped 29%→8.8%, agent immediately wrote manual stdio test scripts (/tmp/test_lsp.py, test_lsp2.py) feeding single initialize/definition/didOpen requests to the server to isolate the root cause — minimal reproduction of individual requests over stdio.

Built dedicated debug scripts (debug_test.py, debug_all.py, debug2.py) that run each LSP method on a specific file (AccessPrivate.java) and diff actual-vs-golden per method, yielding precise field-level findings: selectionRange missing a parent span, semanticTokens wrong legend, prepareCallHierarchy detail field, foldingRange endLine calculation.

Used graduated subset runs (100/2000/5000/10000 entries) to get per-method pass-rate breakdowns (foldingRange 75.5%, references 85.6%, semanticTokens 0%, etc.) rather than a single opaque score, localizing which methods and which exact fields diverge.

Caught the 29%→8.8% regression reactively by re-running tests and diagnosed 4 specific regressions (notification responses, URI format, containerName), but no engineered regression-guard suite was built to prevent future regressions.

Sustained the expected-vs-actual diffing loop late in the trajectory — examining specific source files (FlowValid.java) against golden foldingRange output to pinpoint if-else block span divergences at the line level.

reasoning: The agent went well beyond a pass/fail number: it used run_tests as the outer loop AND built repeated per-method/per-file expected-vs-actual diff scripts, fed individual requests manually over stdio to isolate root causes, and consistently identified the exact divergent field or position (selectionRange parent chain, foldingRange endLine, prepareCallHierarchy detail, semanticTokens legend). This matches the level-8 anchor of a tight verification workflow with targeted single-method/single-request checks. It falls short of 10 because regression guarding was reactive (re-running subsets) rather than engineered infrastructure, and there was no systematic guard ensuring fixed methods stayed fixed.
